narrative.overview:
The site is the coach's tactics board the analysis is drawn on. The ground is white enamel; flat panels are pinned on it one tone step apart; data is drawn on them in two marker inks, Espanyol blue for the team and marker red for the opponent. Nothing has a border or a shadow. Depth comes only from one surface overlapping another: the board rises over the stadium photo, a panel sits on the board, a pill nav floats over both.

The board is calm and dense in the way a real tactics board is: large light figures, short factual lines, and strokes that look drawn by hand (round caps, round joins, straight segments). Each screen has at most one dark panel, a "night" board where the inks lighten so they keep contrast. Exits are numbered only where the order carries information (the depth ladder season, match, possession, player, method).

Pizarra is the new world, built first on the landing (`/`, 24 Oct 2026) and replacing the older design handoff page by page. Light theme only: there is no dark mode, and the night panel is a surface inside the light page, not a theme.
keyCharacteristics: White enamel board, flat tonal panels, no borders, no shadows; depth by overlap only.
Two inks: team (blue) and rival (red); lit versions on the one night panel.
One face, Hanken Grotesk: figures at 300, text at 400 to 500, headings at 600.
Pills for every control; generous radii for board, panel and row.
Data drawn as round-capped marker strokes; a possession draws itself.

rules.name: The Two Inks Rule
rules.body: Every mark on a Pizarra page is team or rival (team-lit or rival-lit on night). A third hue for data is not allowed; distinguish within an ink by fill, opacity, dash or size.

rules.name: The One Night Rule
rules.body: At most one night panel per screen. It is where the signature interaction lives, and its rarity is what makes it read as a second board.

rules.name: The Tone Step Rule
rules.body: Surfaces separate by one lightness step (board, panel, panel-deep, chalk), never by a border. Hover and focus move a surface exactly one step darker.

rules.name: The Light Figure Rule
rules.body: Numbers that matter are large and light (300), never bold. Weight goes to the words that name them.

rules.name: The No Eyebrow Rule
rules.body: No kicker or uppercase label above a heading. Context (season, match count) goes in the line under the heading.

rules.name: The en-GB Numbers Rule
rules.body: The site is in Spanish, but numbers use the decimal point (`en-GB`, `NUMBER_LOCALE` in `web/lib/format.ts`). This is deliberate; do not hand-format numbers.

rules.name: The Overlap-Only Rule
rules.body: If something must read as "above", make it overlap, not cast a shadow. The floating nav is an opaque board-coloured pill over the photo, with no backdrop blur.

dos: **Do** put `.pizarra` on the root element of every page that moves into this world; it sets the face, size, tabular numbers, selection and focus.
**Do** use only the Pizarra tokens (board, panel, panel-deep, chalk, slate, ink, team, rival, night, night-line, night-text, team-lit, rival-lit) and the board / panel / row / pill radii.
**Do** separate surfaces by one tone step and show hover and focus as one step darker.
**Do** draw data as round-capped strokes in the two inks, and remap legacy charts with the chart colour mapping above.
**Do** name the author on every Pizarra page and credit the stadium photo (Elemaki, CC BY 3.0) wherever it appears.
**Do** respect `prefers-reduced-motion`: drawn strokes appear without animating.
donts: **Don't** use borders or shadows on any surface, or backdrop blur on the nav.
**Don't** add a third data colour; carries are dashed team ink, not gold.
**Don't** use more than one night panel on a screen, or add a dark mode.
**Don't** put kickers or uppercase eyebrows above headings, or decorative section numbers; numbers are allowed only where order carries meaning.
**Don't** use Unicode glyphs as icons; use the drawn arrow.
**Don't** use the legacy handoff tokens on a Pizarra page (see below).
